name: VS Code smoke tester
description: Initial static discovery of smoke/ executable code, including mock and real-profile modes.

flows.name: Setting up the smoke test profile
flows.description: Creates or checks the dedicated persistent real-Chat profile, launches a setup window for manual sign-in, and preserves the profile after shutdown. Setup completion does not verify authentication; the real Chat test checks readiness.

transitions.description: Invoke setup:real-chat with the dedicated VS Code build.
Reserve exclusive execution and record ownership of disposable setup resources.
Create a disposable setup workspace and initial fixture.
Create or validate the marked persistent profile; reject mock overrides and require the profile to be closed.
Check platform and build compatibility and launch the dedicated setup window with the real profile and filtered environment.
Load the persistent profile and retain settings and authentication state managed by VS Code.
Complete sign-in manually using the Copilot setup workflow, then close the dedicated window.
Wait for window closure and confirm the owned application shuts down.
Remove owned disposable setup resources after successful shutdown; preserve the persistent profile.

metadata.scope-note: Authentication is manual. Setup writes resource ownership records, not the normal smoke result.json/result.txt reports. Failed or uncertain cleanup retains owned resources for inspection.

flows.name: Smoke test with mock chat service
flows.description: Runs the Chat smoke suite with a disposable synthetic profile and the tester-hosted loopback mock, verifies two exchanges in one fresh local Ask session, then records results and cleans up owned resources.

transitions.description: Invoke the Chat smoke suite with --chat-backend mock (the default).
Reserve exclusive execution and record resource ownership.
Create the disposable workspace and initial fixture.
After compatibility and helper checks, start the in-process mock and prepare disposable settings and synthetic authentication with loopback endpoint overrides.
Launch the dedicated application with the helper, smoke driver, isolated profile, and mock-mode tracing.
Load disposable settings and backend state and write renderer logs.

Open a fresh local Ask session, submit two marked prompts, and observe deterministic replies from the tester-hosted mock. Verify session identity, response counts, completion state, and matching recorded mock requests for each turn.
Read renderer logs to corroborate the active local Chat session identity during verification.
Collect applicable mock failure diagnostics, shut down the owned application, and close the in-process mock.
Remove owned disposable resources on success; retain them on failure or uncertain shutdown.
Write outcome, turn evidence, mock request evidence, timings, cleanup disposition, and applicable failure screenshot or trace.

metadata.scope-note: Chat-only smoke path; optional editing checks are omitted. The mock is internal to smoke-tester. Its loopback requests have no separate relationship in this model, so the Chat execution transition summarizes that exchange. No Github Copilot transition applies.

flows.name: Smoke test with real test service
flows.description: Runs the Chat smoke suite against Github Copilot using the previously configured persistent profile. Verifies an exact token reply and a follow-up recalling that token in the same session, without recording screenshots or traces.

transitions.description: Invoke the Chat smoke suite with --chat-backend real after completing profile setup and closing the setup window.
Reserve exclusive execution and record ownership of disposable run resources.
Create a disposable workspace for the run and temporary Chat exports.
Check the existing persistent profile, ownership, absence of mock overrides, and closed-profile prerequisite; capture the renderer-log baseline.
After compatibility and helper checks, launch the application with the persistent profile and filtered real-backend environment, without screenshots or traces.
Use the persistent profile and existing authentication state; write renderer session logs.
Open a fresh local Ask session, check authentication and Chat readiness, and submit the first marked prompt requesting an exact generated token.
Send the first Chat prompt to the real Copilot service and receive its response.
Export the active test conversation to a temporary workspace file after the first completed response.
Read and verify the exported prompt, exact token, and terminal completion state, then delete the export.
Verify the same session remains active and submit the follow-up asking for the previous token without restating it.
Send the follow-up prompt to the real Copilot service and receive its response.
Export the active two-turn test conversation to a temporary workspace file.
Verify both marked prompts, exact replies, and terminal completion states, then delete the export.
Corroborate local session identity from renderer logs throughout the exchange.
Shut down the owned application after verification or an unsuccessful run.
Remove disposable resources on success; retain failed or uncertain resources while preserving the persistent profile.
Write outcome, test-conversation evidence, timings, and cleanup disposition. Authentication, entitlement, or quota prerequisites produce blocked outcomes; mock request evidence is inapplicable.

metadata.scope-note: Chat-only smoke path; optional editing checks are omitted. Service request/response exchanges are summarized by the existing connects relationship. Sequence numbers order architectural milestones; session-log checks recur during both turns. Failure paths may stop before later transitions.
